# Lago Developer Documentation

> Lago is an open-source, API-first billing platform for usage metering, subscriptions, invoicing, payments, entitlements, and revenue operations. This index is the fastest way for AI agents and developer tools to find authoritative Lago documentation.

## When to use these docs

Use the Lago documentation when you need to evaluate Lago, integrate the REST API, ingest usage events, model pricing, manage customers and subscriptions, generate invoices, coordinate payments, configure webhooks, deploy Lago, or build an AI-assisted billing workflow. Prefer the OpenAPI contract for exact request and response shapes, and prefer task guides for workflow decisions and operational constraints.

Do not invent endpoints, fields, pricing behavior, or permissions. For an exhaustive API contract, use the complete OpenAPI specification. Before any billing mutation, verify the target environment, organization, resource identifiers, currency, effective dates, and authorization. Keep API keys secret. Treat destructive or financial actions as approval-gated.

## Start here

- [Lago Developer Documentation](https://doc.getlago.com/welcome.md): Product orientation, common integration paths, and machine-readable entry points.
- [Developer Resources](https://doc.getlago.com/developers.md): Canonical developer portal for authentication, OpenAPI, SDKs, webhooks, MCP, examples, status, and support.
- [Welcome to Lago](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/introduction/welcome-to-lago.md): Core billing concepts and product model.
- [API Reference](https://doc.getlago.com/api-reference/intro.md): Base URL, authentication, and endpoint reference.
- [API Standards](https://doc.getlago.com/api-reference/api-standards.md): HTTP and payload conventions.
- [Structured Errors](https://doc.getlago.com/api-reference/errors.md): Error status codes and JSON response fields.

## Machine-readable contracts

- [Same-origin OpenAPI discovery schema](https://doc.getlago.com/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 schema for automated discovery, function generation, authentication, and structured errors.
- [Complete production OpenAPI specification](https://swagger.getlago.com/openapi.yaml): Exhaustive Lago REST API contract.
- [OpenAPI source repository](https://github.com/getlago/lago-openapi): Version history and contributions.
- [Sitemap](https://doc.getlago.com/sitemap.xml): Index of published documentation pages.
- [Complete documentation corpus](https://doc.getlago.com/llms-full.txt): Full text export for retrieval and offline context.
- [MCP endpoint](https://doc.getlago.com/mcp): Streamable HTTP endpoint for documentation search and retrieval.
- [MCP guide](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/ai-agents/mcp-server.md): Client configuration and supported capabilities.

## Core billing workflows

- [Ingest usage events](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/events/ingesting-usage.md): Send idempotent product-usage events to Lago.
- [Aggregation types](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/billable-metrics/aggregation-types/overview.md): Count, sum, unique count, latest, maximum, weighted sum, and custom expressions.
- [Plan model](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/plans/plan-model.md): Structure reusable pricing and billing rules.
- [Customers](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/customers/customer-management.md): Model billable customer accounts.
- [Subscriptions](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/subscriptions/assign-plan.md): Attach plans and lifecycle rules to customers.
- [Invoicing](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/invoicing/overview.md): Generate, finalize, and manage invoices.
- [Webhooks](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/webhooks.md): Process asynchronous billing state changes safely.
- [Integration testing](https://doc.getlago.com/guide/integration-testing.md): Validate billing behavior before production rollout.

## Recovery guidance

If a link is missing, search this index first, then the [sitemap](https://doc.getlago.com/sitemap.xml), the [developer portal](https://doc.getlago.com/developers.md), or the [API reference](https://doc.getlago.com/api-reference/intro.md). A documentation 404 does not imply that an API resource or feature is unavailable; verify the complete OpenAPI contract and current product guides before concluding that a capability does not exist.
